definition.def: A chart is a diagram, picture, or graph which is intended to make information easier to understand.
examples: Male unemployment was 14.2%, compared with 5.8% for women (see chart on next page).
The chart below shows our top 10 choices.

definition.def: A chart is a map of the sea or stars.
If you chart an area of land, sea, or sky, or a feature in that area, you make a map of the area or show the feature in it.
examples: Portuguese explorers had charted the west coast of Africa as far as Sierra Leone. [VERB noun]
Ptolemy charted more than 1000 stars in 48 constellations. [VERB noun]
These seas have been well charted. [be VERB-ed]

definition.def: The charts are the official lists that show which songs have had the most downloads or which CDs have sold the most copies each week.
examples: This album confirmed The Orb's status as national stars, going straight to Number One in the charts.
They topped both the U.S. singles and album charts at the same time.

definition.def: If you chart the development or progress of something, you observe it and record or show it. You can also say that a report or graph charts the development or progress of something.
examples: One GP has charted a dramatic rise in local childhood asthma since the motorway was built nearby. [VERB noun]
This magnificent show charts his meteoric rise from 'small town' country singer to top international Rock idol. [VERB noun]
Bulletin boards charted each executive's progress. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If a person or plan charts a course of action, they describe what should be done in order to achieve something or to make progress in the future. [formal]
examples: We've charted a possible way forward. [VERB noun]
NATO had charted a new course for stability and cooperation in Europe. [VERB noun]
Your future is already neatly planned and charted. [VERB noun]
